text: 🇲🇽🎨 "The education budget reached a historic figure: 1.3 trillion pesos." "There are many groups that don't like so many resources going to scholarships. It angers them that young people now have the chance to study, that they are not discriminated against, that they are not called 'ninis' as before." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 The 2027 budget raises education spending by 11%. Scholarships go from 187 to 190 billion pesos. Delgado called reports of cuts "false": the Benito Juárez Well-being Universities rise from 3.105 to 3.205 billion pesos, more than double their 2024 budget. In Zacatecas, every public school student at every level now has a scholarship: 320,893 students and more than 2.142 billion pesos.

🇲🇽🎨 "It's because there aren't enough places. If you had a passing grade in high school, you have the right to a place at university." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 Sheinbaum asked the students how many of every 10 classmates from high school got into university. They shouted 6, 10, 3, 5. "Do you think it's because they didn't pass the admission exam?" "Yes!" "No." Governor David Monreal estimates about 10,000 young people in Zacatecas are left out of university, so the Rosario Castellanos National University campus under construction there will be built for 10,000 students, "so that nobody is left without studying university." She toured the construction site after the event.

🇲🇽🔍 "If the education system had not been abandoned for years, there would not be the violence there is in the country. I can assure you of that." "The only way to address the cause that leads young people to approach a criminal group is to give them education and give them a scholarship. Where should young people be, on the street or in school?" — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Well-being Scholarships event, Villanueva, Zacatecas, Nov 21, 2026 "What do we have to do? Give them support so they stay in school, and also build more schools, because for years schools stopped being built." Sheinbaum spoke to high school and university students receiving the Benito Juárez and Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarships.
